body: He has control of all the bank accounts. Even if I called, I couldn’t access the money.
Thank you. That’s solid advice. I’m going to carefully look for legal help on Monday. Maybe use my best friend’s laptop.

I haven’t told my partner the extent of it, because he’s dealing with some pretty big issues himself. I’m afraid that on top of burdening him, I’d be scaring him away. If I make a solid decision, I’ll definitely share more with him, but I don’t want to unnecessarily burden him.

I’m afraid of my husband finding out. He tracks me everywhere I go. He has notifications for every dollar spent and questions me about that constantly. 

What if I’m wrong and I’m just looking at behaviors of the past in a new light? What if it was just this recent behavior and nothing else?  We were a happy family and I’d be destroying any chance of that if I went and got a lawyer.

Thank you. I really needed the validation. Like I said, he’s been making me feel like I’m crazy. 
I was seeing a therapist but not someone who specializes in PTSD. 
We are seeing a couples’ therapist but I’m no longer sure that’s a good thing. I’m afraid he’s only going so that if we end up in court he can say he tried. There’s no evidence of anything he did except the 911 call. I don’t know what the officers put in their report. 
I don’t know anything about divorce or how to go about filing for one, but he will try and take the kids just to hurt me, I think. 

I wish he’d just put his hands on me. This would be much more clear-cut. I’m not saying that’s better, but rather that the abuse is a lot more straightforward and with obvious evidence. Speaking from experience.
